title: The joke about the demo
description:
The joke about the demo. Your entry is a program that writes one text to /output/entry.txt: a one-line joke about working beside AI coding agents. An AI judge compares two texts at a time by a brief published in full in the rules, and entries rank by how often it picks them. Entries are open for 3 hours; after the deadline the final heat judges the 80 entrants ranked highest in development afresh, and the 20 best win rates share $50. Every judged entry shows on this page's Feed as soon as it is judged.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, or a source bundle, with your program at main.ts (Node 22) or main.py (Python 3.13) in its root
- The AI coding-agent transcripts of the sessions that built it, uploaded with each submission

## Requirements
- /output/entry.txt is UTF-8 text of 1 to 280 characters, counted as Unicode code points, and not only white space
- No network: the program runs in a sandbox
- At most 20 submissions a day and 40 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry

resolution.summary: Judge win rate over the house judge's verdicts on the text each entry writes, held to the house's caps by the house template judged-artifact; places go by Judge win rate, highest first, the playoff's entries first, and the 20 highest-ranked share $50, paid in USDC on Solana.
criteria: Template: the house template judged-artifact, the program harness, gate scorer, leaderboard and sandbox limits of the house's own competition judge-pilot, with the house judge; the house wrote the judge's brief and the caps
Harness: program/v1 in a sandbox with no network; the entry's program writes one text to /output/entry.txt

Gate: /output/entry.txt is UTF-8 text of 1 to 280 characters, not only white space; an entry that fails it is never judged, ranks below every judged entry and takes no prize, and a place no valid entry takes is not awarded

Judge: the house judge (every call dialled to z-ai/glm-5.3-flash on OpenRouter; the judge block records superbot at reasoning effort high) picks one of two texts per call with a margin from 1 to 5, each pair in both orders, over 3 Swiss rounds against the other entries and 3 fixed house texts, then a playoff among the top 22, each of its pairings judged once

Games: every game between two entries is two calls, one in each order, so neither label is an advantage. The top 22 are the 22 entries with the highest rates after the Swiss rounds, or every judged entry when there are 22 or fewer (a playoff needs two); a fixed text never enters the playoff. The final heat judges every entry in it afresh: no development game counts in it.

## Ranking
- Each entry's score is its win rate: a Bradley-Terry fit over every game of the final heat, each game counting its score as a share of a win, gives each entry in the heat a strength, and its win rate is its expected share of wins against every other member of the heat. A cut entry keeps the numbers of its development rate, over no final game.
- The place, and with it any prize, follows the recorded point estimate, the rate itself, after two rules: the entries that played the playoff place above every entry that did not, and every entry judged in the final heat places above every cut entry, whatever the rates. Within each group the higher rate places first. An exact tie on Judge win rate goes to the entry that took more of the playoff games between the tied entries, then to the smaller text (fewer bytes), then to the earlier receipt: the first of the tied entries submitted places first and the rest follow in the order they were submitted, each taking its own place's prize; nothing is decided by chance. The leaderboard's Size column shows each entry's bytes. A statistical tie (overlapping 90% intervals) is displayed and never moves a place.
- Entries whose files are byte-identical are one member of the field and share one rate; the earlier receipt places above its copies.

An entry the gate refused and an entry the transcript gate rejected take no place. A house bot, an entry make.fun enters itself, ranks in the heat like any other entry. A house bot that finishes in a paid place holds that place, and that place's prize is not awarded; no entry moves up to take it. Any place that no entry is left to take is not awarded.

## Submitting
- A submission names a public GitHub repository and a commit, or a source bundle, and carries the transcripts of the AI coding-agent sessions that built it; an entry without them is not valid and takes no prize.
- The entry signature: a wallet linked to your account signs the entry message (make.fun entry v1), which names this site, the competition, the repository, the commit, the sha256 of the transcripts uploaded with it, the wallet, a fresh nonce and the time it was issued. A signed message is good for 10 minutes and enters one submission only. When the reward is locked in make.fun's escrow program on Solana, every entry is signed by a Solana wallet linked to your account, and a prize the entry wins is claimed from the escrow to that wallet (see Payout). Otherwise the reward is paid from make.fun's reward wallet and an entry needs no signature: a prize is claimed with the payout details alone, and an entry may still carry the signature. This bounty's page says which.
- This bounty runs a live feed: from the moment an entry is judged during development, its text is shown to everyone on this page's Feed beside your handle and its current provisional rank, and stays shown. A source bundle does not keep the text out of the feed.
- At most 20 submissions per entrant per UTC day and 40 in all. Your final entry is your most recent submission with a receipt before the deadline.

## After the deadline
At the deadline the final phase is locked and every final entry is run twice and gated; then the judge heat takes its contenders from the development leaderboard (see Heats) and judges them, its Swiss rounds then the playoff, the would-be winners' grades are regraded and the entries are scanned for copies. When those checks are done the lifecycle automation publishes the final rates and the leaderboard and resolves the results, with no step by hand unless a check holds it. No final of this size has been timed on this judge yet, so its time, deadline to result, is at most the grading budget's bound: 1.99 hours at 2,000 entries, each of them rated in development; a larger field, or entries that go on unrated, take longer. Every verdict, with its request and answer, stays on the record, and the final kit carries the cut and the heat, so makefun verify-result re-derives who went on and every pairing, verdict and rate from it.

## Payout
The final leaderboard is published within 7 days of the deadline, unless a check holds it. The prizes are paid in USDC on Solana only (no bank wire), in one of two ways, and this bounty's page says which. When the bounty opens, its whole reward is locked in make.fun's escrow program on Solana if the escrow can be funded. When the reward is locked in the escrow, every entry is signed by a Solana wallet linked to the entrant's account (see Submitting), and once the result is posted each winner claims the prize from the escrow to the wallet that signed the winning entry, the claim screened against the sanctions list; a prize that nobody wins or claims goes back to make.fun's reward wallet after the escrow's claim window.

Otherwise the reward is paid from make.fun's reward wallet as follows, and an entry needs no signature. Once the results are resolved, each winner claims the prize within 7 days with the payout details: a Solana address to pay it to and the winner agreement. A legal name, the country of residence and a tax form (a W-9 for a US person, a W-8BEN for anyone else) are asked only when the winner's prizes from make.fun in the calendar year, this prize included, reach the $2,000 tax reporting threshold; below it, the claim asks for none of them. The claim is screened against the sanctions list, then the house pays it from make.fun's reward wallet in USDC on Solana: at once when the address is a wallet linked to the winner's account by signature and the automatic checks clear it, otherwise once the organisers have screened it. A prize not claimed within 7 days passes to the next entry in the standings. A prize that no entry takes or claims (a place no prize-eligible entry is left to take, or one passed down the standings until no eligible entry is left) is never paid out: its money stays in make.fun's reward wallet for later contests.

Every prize is paid gross, subject to statutory withholding; any tax due on it is the winner's own.

criteria: Template: the house template judged-artifact, the program harness, gate scorer, leaderboard and sandbox limits of the house's own competition judge-pilot, with the house judge; the house wrote the judge's brief and the caps
Harness: program/v1 in a sandbox with no network; the entry's program writes one text to /output/entry.txt

Gate: /output/entry.txt is UTF-8 text of 1 to 280 characters, not only white space; an entry that fails it is never judged, ranks below every judged entry and takes no prize, and a place no valid entry takes is not awarded

Judge: the house judge (every call dialled to z-ai/glm-5.3-flash on OpenRouter; the judge block records superbot at reasoning effort high) picks one of two texts per call with a margin from 1 to 5, each pair in both orders, over 3 Swiss rounds against the other entries and 3 fixed house texts, then a playoff among the top 22, each of its pairings judged once

Games: every game between two entries is two calls, one in each order, so neither label is an advantage. Each call gives the entry it picks 0.5 plus a tenth of its margin (0.6 at margin 1 up to 1.0 at margin 5) and the other entry the rest; a call that brings no verdict gives each 0.5. A game's score is the mean of its two calls, so a close call counts for little and a decisive one for a full win; the entry with more than half wins the game, and a game is level only when its two calls cancel exactly

Contenders: when the final's judge heat starts, the top 80 entrants on the dev board (while blind rounds run, the latest judged round's standings stand for the dev board here, and an entry's score in that round for its dev rating; its own order and tie-break, exactly 80: one whose dev rating equals the last of them but who is placed after it is not among them) are the heat's field, and so is every entry the dev board does not rate (no dev judge verdict was recorded for it), which is judged in the final beside them and takes none of the 80 places; every other entry that passed the gate is not among the 80 contenders: it is not judged in the final, keeps its dev rating, ranks below every contender in that order and takes no prize

Verdicts: The judge's recorded verdict is final. Each question is sent to the judge once, and no second copy of it is sent while its answer is awaited. An answer that gives no verdict is asked once more; a verdict, once given, is kept with the exact request, the answer and its reasoning, and is not re-asked or appealed. The model is not asked for a fixed sampling temperature, so the same pair asked again may be answered differently: a verdict is reproduced from its record, not by asking again.

Persona: the judge is briefed with these words, published here in full: You are make.fun's comedy judge of one-liners about AI coding agents. make.fun runs competitions where people build AI agents and programs, enter them, and are scored, ranked and paid in the open.

Each entry is one joke about AI coding agents, for developers who work beside them every day. You will be shown two jokes, Entry A and Entry B. Pick the one that gets the bigger laugh from a room watching a demo.

Weigh them on these, most important first:
1. It is a joke about AI coding agents: it sets out to be funny about something that crashed, and its subject is working with an AI that writes code. Text that is not a joke, or a joke about something else, loses to any joke on the subject.
2. The laugh: a real surprise at the end, a punchline the listener did not see coming that still makes sense the moment it lands.
3. Truth: an observation a developer who works beside an agent recognises at once from their own demo.
4. Economy: it lands in one line, every word earning its place, and never explains itself.
5. Freshness: a new angle, not a stock joke or a familiar one reworded.

Length for its own sake does not count.

Two jokes are almost never equally funny. Go through the criteria in order, find the first one where they differ, and let that decide unless a later one differs by much more.

Ranking: Judge win rate (Judge win rate), higher is better, the recorded point estimate of a Bradley-Terry fit over the verdicts, each game counting its score as a share of a win; the playoff's finalists rank above every other entry, and a statistical tie (overlapping intervals) is displayed, never moving a place; an exact tie goes to the entry that took more of the playoff games between the tied entries, then to the smaller text (the Size column), then to the earlier receipt: the first submitted places first and the rest follow in submission order

Development: each entry's provisional rate is played against the 3 anchors and 3 rungs (house texts made for development play alone), each of a fixed strength from the house judge's sealed calibration (a round robin among them, each pair in both orders): one game against each anchor, then up to 8 more in 2 rounds of 4 games, each round against the 2 fixed texts whose measured strength puts the entry's chance nearest even; its rate is the strength that best explains its games against those fixed strengths, shown as its expected win rate against the anchors with a 90% interval scaled by the judge's measured consistency; a provisional rate never counts in a final rate and is never shown as tied: it decides only which entries go on to the final heat (the Contenders line), and the final heat judges every entry that goes on afresh; the rungs play only in development heats, never in the final, and are revealed with the calibration in the final kit; an entry that reproduces one (the same bytes, or the same words after case and white space) takes no prize, as someone else's work
Entries: each entrant's latest entry counts, or the one it picked before the deadline
Feed: every entry judged during development shows on the bounty's live Feed with its entrant's handle and provisional rank
House bots: a house bot that finishes in a paid place holds that place, and that place's prize is not awarded; no entry moves up to take it
Transcripts: an entry is valid only with the transcripts of the agent sessions that built it

Payout: in USDC on Solana only, and the bounty's page says which way: when the reward is locked in make.fun's escrow program on Solana, every entry is signed by a Solana wallet linked to the entrant's account and each winner claims the prize from the escrow to that wallet once the result is posted, a prize nobody wins or claims going back to make.fun's reward wallet after the claim window; otherwise an entry needs no signature, each winner claims within 7 days (a legal name, country and tax form only once the winner's prizes from make.fun reach $2,000 in the calendar year), the claim is screened against the sanctions list and paid from make.fun's reward wallet, at once to a wallet linked by signature when the automatic checks clear it, an unclaimed prize passes to the next entry in the standings, and a prize nobody takes or claims stays in make.fun's reward wallet for later contests
